a keeper of the great seer’s treasury,
is a visionary for the whole world,
learned and honorable.

17.3.s:
Dhammārāmo dhammarato,
dhammaṁ anuvicintayaṁ;
Dhammaṁ anussaraṁ bhikkhu,
saddhammā na parihāyati.
17.3.e:
Delighting in the teaching, enjoying the teaching,
contemplating the teaching,
a mendicant who recollects the teaching
doesn’t fall away from the true teaching.”

17.3.s:
Kāyamaccheragaruno,
hiyyamāne anuṭṭhahe;
Sarīrasukhagiddhassa,
kuto samaṇaphāsutā.
17.3.e:
“When your body is pampered and heavy,
while your remaining time is running out,
greedy for physical pleasure,
how can you be comfortable as an ascetic?”

17.3.s:
Na pakkhanti disā sabbā,
dhammā na paṭibhanti maṁ;
Gate kalyāṇamittamhi,
andhakāraṁva khāyati.
17.3.e:
“I’m completely disorientated!
The teachings don’t spring to mind!
With the passing of our good friend,
everything seems dark.

17.3.s:
Abbhatītasahāyassa,
atītagatasatthuno;
Natthi etādisaṁ mittaṁ,
yathā kāyagatā sati.
17.3.e:
When your friend has passed away,
and your Teacher is past and gone,
there’s no friend like
mindfulness of the body.

17.3.s:
Ye purāṇā atītā te,
navehi na sameti me;
Svajja ekova jhāyāmi,
vassupetova pakkhimā”.
17.3.e:
The old have passed away,
and I don’t agree with the new.
Today I meditate alone
like a bird snug in its nest.”

17.3.s:
“Dassanāya abhikkante,
nānāverajjake bahū;
Mā vārayittha sotāro,
passantu samayo mamaṁ”.
17.3.e:
“Many visitors from abroad
have come to visit.
Don’t block the audience,
let the congregation see me.”

17.3.s:
“Dassanāya abhikkante,
nānāverajjake puthu;
Karoti satthā okāsaṁ,
na nivāreti cakkhumā.
17.3.e:
“Lots of visitors from abroad
have come to visit.
The teacher grants them the opportunity,
the Clear-eyed One doesn’t turn them away.”

17.3.s:
Paṇṇavīsativassāni,
sekhabhūtassa me sato;
Na kāmasaññā uppajji,
passa dhammasudhammataṁ.
17.3.e:
“In the twenty five years that have passed
since I became a trainee,
no sensual perception has arisen in me:
behold the clear rightness of the teaching!

17.3.s:
Paṇṇavīsativassāni,
sekhabhūtassa me sato;
Na dosasaññā uppajji,
passa dhammasudhammataṁ.
17.3.e:
In the twenty-five years
since I became a trainee,
no malicious perception has arisen in me:
behold the clear rightness of the teaching!”

17.3.s:
Paṇṇavīsativassāni,
bhagavantaṁ upaṭṭhahiṁ;
Mettena kāyakammena,
chāyāva anapāyinī.
17.3.e:
“For twenty-five years
I attended on the Buddha
with loving deeds,
like a shadow that never left.

17.3.s:
Paṇṇavīsativassāni,
bhagavantaṁ upaṭṭhahiṁ;
Mettena vacīkammena,
chāyāva anapāyinī.
17.3.e:
For twenty-five years
I attended on the Buddha
with loving words,
like a shadow that never left.

17.3.s:
Paṇṇavīsativassāni,
bhagavantaṁ upaṭṭhahiṁ;
Mettena manokammena,
chāyāva anapāyinī.
17.3.e:
For twenty-five years
I attended on the Buddha
with loving thoughts,
like a shadow that never left.

17.3.s:
Buddhassa caṅkamantassa,
piṭṭhito anucaṅkamiṁ;
Dhamme desiyamānamhi,
ñāṇaṁ me udapajjatha.
17.3.e:
While the Buddha was walking mindfully,
I walked behind him.
As he taught the Dhamma,
knowledge arose in me.”

17.3.s:
Ahaṁ sakaraṇīyomhi,
sekho appattamānaso;
Satthu ca parinibbānaṁ,
yo amhaṁ anukampako.
17.3.e:
“I’m a trainee, who has more to do;
my heart’s desire is still unfulfilled.
Yet the Teacher, who was so compassionate to me,
has become fully extinguished.

17.3.s:
Tadāsi yaṁ bhiṁsanakaṁ,
tadāsi lomahaṁsanaṁ;
Sabbākāravarūpete,
sambuddhe parinibbute”.
17.3.e:
Then there was terror!
Then they had goosebumps!
When the Buddha, endowed with all fine qualities,
was fully quenched.”

17.3.s:
“Bahussuto dhammadharo,
kosārakkho mahesino;
Cakkhu sabbassa lokassa,
ānando parinibbuto.
17.3.e:
“Ānanda, who was learned <j>and had memorized the teaching,
a keeper of the great seer’s treasury,
a visionary for the entire world,
has become fully quenched.

17.3.s:
Bahussuto dhammadharo,
kosārakkho mahesino;
Cakkhu sabbassa lokassa,
andhakāre tamonudo.
17.3.e:
He was learned <j>and had memorized the teaching,
a keeper of the great seer’s treasury,
a visionary for the entire world,
in thick of night he dispelled the dark.

17.3.s:
Gatimanto satimanto,
dhitimanto ca yo isi;
Saddhammadhārako thero,
ānando ratanākaro”.
17.3.e:
He is the seer who remembered the teachings,
and mastered their sequence, holding them firm.
The senior monk who memorized the teaching,
Ānanda was a mine of gems.”

17.3.s:
“Pariciṇṇo mayā satthā,
kataṁ buddhassa sāsanaṁ;
Ohito garuko bhāro,
natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.
17.3.e:
“I’ve served the Teacher
and fulfilled the Buddha’s instructions.
The heavy burden is laid down,
now there’ll be no more future lives.”

18.1.s:
“Na gaṇena purakkhato care,
Vimano hoti samādhi dullabho;
Nānājanasaṅgaho dukho,
Iti disvāna gaṇaṁ na rocaye.
18.1.e:
“You shouldn’t live for the adulation of a following;
it turns your mind, making it hard to get immersion.
Seeing that popularity is suffering,
you shouldn’t consent to a following.

18.1.s:
Na kulāni upabbaje muni,
Vimano hoti samādhi dullabho;
So ussukko rasānugiddho,
Atthaṁ riñcati yo sukhāvaho.
18.1.e:
A sage should not visit respectable families;
it turns your mind, making it hard to get immersion.
If you’re eager and greedy for flavors,
you’ll miss the goal that brings such happiness.

18.1.s:
Paṅkoti hi naṁ avedayuṁ,
Yāyaṁ vandanapūjanā kulesu;
Sukhumaṁ sallaṁ durubbahaṁ,
Sakkāro kāpurisena dujjaho.
18.1.e:
They know it really is a bog,
this homage and veneration in respectable families.
Honor is a subtle dart, hard to extract,
and hard for a reprobate to give up.”

18.1.s:
Senāsanamhā oruyha,
nagaraṁ piṇḍāya pāvisiṁ;
Bhuñjantaṁ purisaṁ kuṭṭhiṁ,
sakkaccaṁ taṁ upaṭṭhahiṁ.
18.1.e:
“I came down from my lodging
and entered the city for alms.
I courteously stood by
while a leper ate.

18.1.s:
So me pakkena hatthena,
ālopaṁ upanāmayi;
Ālopaṁ pakkhipantassa,
aṅguli cettha chijjatha.
18.1.e:
With his putrid hand
he offered me a morsel.
Putting the morsel in my bowl,
his finger dropped off right there.

18.1.s:
Kuṭṭamūlañca nissāya,
ālopaṁ taṁ abhuñjisaṁ;
Bhuñjamāne vā bhutte vā,
jegucchaṁ me na vijjati.
18.1.e:
Sitting by a wall,
I ate that lump of rice.
I did not feel any disgust
while eating or afterwards.

Anyone who makes use of
leftovers for food,
rancid urine as medicine,
the root of a tree as lodging,
and cast-off rags as robes,
is at ease in any quarter.”

18.1.s:
Piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto,
selamāruyha kassapo;
Jhāyati anupādāno,
pahīnabhayabheravo.
18.1.e:
Returning from almsround,
Kassapa ascends the mountain,
and practices absorption without grasping,
with fear and dread given up.

18.1.s:
Piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto,
selamāruyha kassapo;
Jhāyati anupādāno,
ḍayhamānesu nibbuto.
18.1.e:
Returning from almsround,
Kassapa ascends the mountain,
and practices absorption without grasping,
quenched amongst those who burn.

18.1.s:
Piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto,
selamāruyha kassapo;
Jhāyati anupādāno,
katakicco anāsavo.
18.1.e:
Returning from almsround,
Kassapa ascends the mountain,
and practices absorption without grasping,
his task completed, free of defilements.”

18.1.s:
Karerimālāvitatā,
bhūmibhāgā manoramā;
Kuñjarābhirudā rammā,
te selā ramayanti maṁ.
18.1.e:
“Strewn with garlands of the musk-rose tree,
these regions are so delightful, so lovely,
echoing with the trumpeting of elephants:
these rocky crags delight me!

18.1.s:
Nīlabbhavaṇṇā rucirā,
vārisītā sucindharā;
Indagopakasañchannā,
te selā ramayanti maṁ.
18.1.e:
Glistening, they look like blue stormclouds,
with waters cool and streams so clear,
and covered all in ladybugs:
these rocky crags delight me!

18.1.s:
Nīlabbhakūṭasadisā,
kūṭāgāravarūpamā;
Vāraṇābhirudā rammā,
te selā ramayanti maṁ.
18.1.e:
Like the peak of a blue stormcloud,
or like a fine bungalow, lovely,
echoing with the trumpeting of elephants:
these rocky crags delight me!

18.1.s:
Abhivuṭṭhā rammatalā,
nagā isibhi sevitā;
Abbhunnaditā sikhīhi,
te selā ramayanti maṁ.
18.1.e:
The rain comes down on the lovely flats,
in the mountains frequented by seers.
Echoing with the cries of peacocks,
these rocky crags delight me!

18.1.s:
Alaṁ jhāyitukāmassa,
pahitattassa me sato;
Alaṁ me atthakāmassa,
pahitattassa bhikkhuno.
18.1.e:
It’s enough for me, who loves absorption,
to remain resolute.
It’s enough for me,
a resolute monk who wants what’s best.

18.1.s:
Alaṁ me phāsukāmassa,
pahitattassa bhikkhuno;
Alaṁ me yogakāmassa,
pahitattassa tādino.
18.1.e:
It’s enough for me,
a resolute monk who loves comfort.
It’s enough for me,
resolute and unaffected, loving meditation.

18.1.s:
Umāpupphena samānā,
gaganāvabbhachāditā;
Nānādijagaṇākiṇṇā,
te selā ramayanti maṁ.
18.1.e:
Covered with flowers of flax,
like the welkin covered with stormclouds,
full of flocks of many different birds,
these rocky crags delight me!

18.1.s:
Anākiṇṇā gahaṭṭhehi,
migasaṅghanisevitā;
Nānādijagaṇākiṇṇā,
te selā ramayanti maṁ.
18.1.e:
Empty of householders,
frequented by herds of deer,
full of flocks of many different birds,
these rocky crags delight me!

18.1.s:
Acchodikā puthusilā,
gonaṅgulamigāyutā;
Ambusevālasañchannā,
te selā ramayanti maṁ.
18.1.e:
The water’s clear and the rocks are broad,
monkeys and deer are all around;
festooned with dewy moss,
these rocky crags delight me!”

18.1.s:
Na pañcaṅgikena turiyena,
Rati me hoti tādisī;
Yathā ekaggacittassa,
Sammā dhammaṁ vipassato.
18.1.e:
“Even the music of a five-piece band
can never give such pleasure
as when, with unified mind,
you rightly discern the Dhamma.”

18.1.s:
Kammaṁ bahukaṁ na kāraye,
Parivajjeyya janaṁ na uyyame;
Ussukko so rasānugiddho,
Atthaṁ riñcati yo sukhāvaho.
18.1.e:
“Don’t get involved in lots of work,
avoid people, and don’t try to acquire things.
If you’re eager and greedy for flavors,
you’ll miss the goal that brings such happiness.

18.1.s:
Kammaṁ bahukaṁ na kāraye,
Parivajjeyya anattaneyyametaṁ;
Kicchati kāyo kilamati,
Dukkhito so samathaṁ na vindati.
18.1.e:
Don’t get involved in lots of work,
avoid what doesn’t lead to the goal.
The body gets worn out and fatigued,
and when you ache, you won’t find serenity.”

18.1.s:
Oṭṭhappahatamattena,
attānampi na passati;
Patthaddhagīvo carati,
ahaṁ seyyoti maññati.
18.1.e:
“You won’t see yourself
by merely reciting words,
wandering stiff-necked
and thinking, ‘I’m better than them.’

18.1.s:
Aseyyo seyyasamānaṁ,
bālo maññati attānaṁ;
Na taṁ viññū pasaṁsanti,
patthaddhamānasaṁ naraṁ.
18.1.e:
The fool is no better,
but they think they are.
The wise don’t praise
pompous people.

18.1.s:
Yo ca seyyohamasmīti,
nāhaṁ seyyoti vā pana;
Hīno taṁsadiso vāti,
vidhāsu na vikampati.
18.1.e:
Whoever does not waver
due to the discriminations—
‘I am better’, ‘I’m not better’,
‘I am worse’, or ‘I am the same’—

18.1.s:
Paññavantaṁ tathā tādiṁ,
sīlesu susamāhitaṁ;
Cetosamathamanuttaṁ,
tañce viññū pasaṁsare.
18.1.e:
with such understanding, unaffected,
steady in ethics,
and devoted to serenity of mind:
that is who the wise praise.”

18.1.s:
Yassa sabrahmacārīsu,
gāravo nūpalabbhati;
Ārakā hoti saddhammā,
nabhato puthavī yathā.
18.1.e:
“Whoever has no respect
for their spiritual companions
is as far from the true teaching
as the earth is from the sky.

18.1.s:
Yesañca hiriottappaṁ,
sadā sammā upaṭṭhitaṁ;
Virūḷhabrahmacariyā te,
tesaṁ khīṇā punabbhavā.
18.1.e:
Those whose conscience and prudence
are always rightly established,
thrive in the spiritual life;
for them, there are no future lives.

18.1.s:
Uddhato capalo bhikkhu,
paṁsukūlena pāruto;
Kapīva sīhacammena,
na so tenupasobhati.
18.1.e:
When a mendicant who is haughty and fickle
wears rags from the rubbish-heap,
that doesn’t make them shine:
they’re like a monkey in a lion skin.

18.1.s:
Anuddhato acapalo,
nipako saṁvutindriyo;
Sobhati paṁsukūlena,
sīhova girigabbhare.
18.1.e:
But if they not restless or fickle,
alert, with senses restrained,
then, wearing rags from the rubbish-heap, they shine
like a lion in a mountain cave.”

18.1.s:
Ete sambahulā devā,
iddhimanto yasassino;
Dasadevasahassāni,
sabbe te brahmakāyikā.
18.1.e:
“These many gods
powerful and glorious,
all 10,000 of them,
belong to the host of the Divinity.

18.1.s:
Dhammasenāpatiṁ vīraṁ,
mahājhāyiṁ samāhitaṁ;
Sāriputtaṁ namassantā,
tiṭṭhanti pañjalīkatā.
18.1.e:
They stand with cupped palms
honoring Sāriputta,
the General of the Dhamma, the hero,
the serene great meditator:

18.1.s:
‘Namo te purisājañña,
namo te purisuttama;
Yassa te nābhijānāma,
yampi nissāya jhāyati.
18.1.e:
‘Homage to you, O thoroughbred!
Homage to you, supreme among men!
We don’t understand
the basis of your absorption.

18.1.s:
Accheraṁ vata buddhānaṁ,
gambhīro gocaro sako;
Ye mayaṁ nābhijānāma,
vālavedhisamāgatā’.
18.1.e:
The profound domain of the Buddhas
is truly amazing.
We don’t understand,
though we’ve gathered here to split hairs.’

18.1.s:
Taṁ tathā devakāyehi,
pūjitaṁ pūjanārahaṁ;
Sāriputtaṁ tadā disvā,
kappinassa sitaṁ ahu.
18.1.e:
When he saw the host of gods
paying homage to Sāriputta—
who is truly worthy of homage—
Kappina smiled.”

18.1.s:
Yāvatā buddhakhettamhi,
ṭhapayitvā mahāmuniṁ;
Dhutaguṇe visiṭṭhohaṁ,
sadiso me na vijjati.
18.1.e:
“As far as the range of the Buddha extends,
apart from the great sage himself,
I am distinguished in austerities,
no equal to me is found.

18.1.s:
Pariciṇṇo mayā satthā,
kataṁ buddhassa sāsanaṁ;
Ohito garuko bhāro,
natthi dāni punabbhavo.
18.1.e:
I’ve served the Teacher
and fulfilled the Buddha’s instructions.
The heavy burden is laid down,
now there’ll be no more future lives.”

“Like a lotus flower
to which water will not stick,
Gotama the immeasurable is unstained
by robes, lodgings, or food.
He inclines to renunciation,
and has escaped the three states of existence.

18.1.s:
Satipaṭṭhānagīvo so,
saddhāhattho mahāmuni;
Paññāsīso mahāñāṇī,
sadā carati nibbuto”ti.
18.1.e:
The great sage’s neck is mindfulness meditation;
faith is his hands, and wisdom his head.
Having great knowledge,
he always wanders, quenched.”

19.1.s:
“Kadā nuhaṁ pabbatakandarāsu,
Ekākiyo addutiyo vihassaṁ;
Aniccato sabbabhavaṁ vipassaṁ,
Taṁ me idaṁ taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I stay in a mountain cave,
alone, with no companion,
discerning all states of existence as impermanent?
This hope of mine, <j>when will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nuhaṁ bhinnapaṭandharo muni,
Kāsāvavattho amamo nirāso;
Rāgañca dosañca tatheva mohaṁ,
Hantvā sukhī pavanagato vihassaṁ.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I stay happily in the forest,
a sage wearing a torn robe, dressed in ocher,
unselfish, with no need for hope,
with greed, hate, and delusion destroyed?

19.1.s:
Kadā aniccaṁ vadharoganīḷaṁ,
Kāyaṁ imaṁ maccujarāyupaddutaṁ;
Vipassamāno vītabhayo vihassaṁ,
Eko vane taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I stay alone in the wood,
fearless, discerning this body as impermanent,
a nest of death and disease,
harried by death and old age; when will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nuhaṁ bhayajananiṁ dukhāvahaṁ,
Taṇhālataṁ bahuvidhānuvattaniṁ;
Paññāmayaṁ tikhiṇamasiṁ gahetvā,
Chetvā vase tampi kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I live, <j>having grasped the sharp sword of wisdom
and cut the creeper of craving <j>that tangles around everything,
the mother of fear, the bringer of suffering?
When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nu paññāmayamuggatejaṁ,
Satthaṁ isīnaṁ sahasādiyitvā;
Māraṁ sasenaṁ sahasā bhañjissaṁ,
Sīhāsane taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I, seated on the lion’s throne,
swiftly grasp the sword of the seers,
forged by wisdom, of awesome might,
and swiftly break Māra and his army? <j>When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nuhaṁ sabbhi samāgamesu,
Diṭṭho bhave dhammagarūhi tādibhi;
Yāthāvadassīhi jitindriyehi,
Padhāniyo taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I be seen in the assemblies
with those who are virtuous, unaffected, <j>respecting the Dhamma,
seeing things as they are, with faculties subdued?
When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nu maṁ tandi khudā pipāsā,
Vātātapā kīṭasarīsapā vā;
Na bādhayissanti na taṁ giribbaje,
Atthatthiyaṁ taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I focus on my heart’s goal <j>in the Mountainfold,
free of oppression by laziness, hunger, thirst,
wind, heat, bugs, and reptiles?
When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nu kho yaṁ viditaṁ mahesinā,
Cattāri saccāni sududdasāni;
Samāhitatto satimā agacchaṁ,
Paññāya taṁ taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I, serene and mindful,
understand the four truths,
that were realized by the great seer,
and are so very hard to see? <j>When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nu rūpe amite ca sadde,
Gandhe rase phusitabbe ca dhamme;
Ādittatohaṁ samathehi yutto,
Paññāya dacchaṁ tadidaṁ kadā me.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I, devoted to serenity,
see with understanding the infinite sights,
sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas
as burning? <j>When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nuhaṁ dubbacanena vutto,
Tato nimittaṁ vimano na hessaṁ;
Atho pasatthopi tato nimittaṁ,
Tuṭṭho na hessaṁ tadidaṁ kadā me.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I not be distraught
because of criticism,
nor elated because of praise?
When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nu kaṭṭhe ca tiṇe latā ca,
Khandhe imehaṁ amite ca dhamme;
Ajjhattikāneva ca bāhirāni ca,
Samaṁ tuleyyaṁ tadidaṁ kadā me.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I discern the aggregates
and the infinite varieties of phenomena,
those interior and exterior, as no more than
wood, grass, and creepers? <j>When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nu maṁ pāvusakālamegho,
Navena toyena sacīvaraṁ vane;
Isippayātamhi pathe vajantaṁ,
Ovassate taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will the monsoon clouds in season
freshly wet me in my robe in the forest,
walking the path trodden by the seers?
When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā mayūrassa sikhaṇḍino vane,
Dijassa sutvā girigabbhare rutaṁ;
Paccuṭṭhahitvā amatassa pattiyā,
Sañcintaye taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I rise up, <j>intent on attaining freedom from death,
hearing, in the mountain cave,
the cry of the crested peacock in the forest?
When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nu gaṅgaṁ yamunaṁ sarassatiṁ,
Pātālakhittaṁ vaḷavāmukhañca;
Asajjamāno patareyyamiddhiyā,
Vibhiṁsanaṁ taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I cross by psychic power unobstructed
the Ganges, Yamunā, and Sarasvatī;
and that place where one is thrown in the abyss,
the horrifying Mare’s Mouth? When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā nu nāgova asaṅgacārī,
Padālaye kāmaguṇesu chandaṁ;
Nibbajjayaṁ sabbasubhaṁ nimittaṁ,
Jhāne yuto taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I be devoted to absorption,
shunning all the signs of beauty,
splitting apart desire for sensual stimulation,
like an elephant that wanders free of ties? <j>When will it be?

19.1.s:
Kadā iṇaṭṭova daliddako nidhiṁ,
Ārādhayitvā dhanikehi pīḷito;
Tuṭṭho bhavissaṁ adhigamma sāsanaṁ,
Mahesino taṁ nu kadā bhavissati.
19.1.e:
Oh, when will I realize the teaching of the great seer
and be content, like a pauper in debt
harassed by creditors, who finds a hidden treasure?
When will it be?

19.1.s:
Bahūni vassāni tayāmhi yācito,
‘Agāravāsena alaṁ nu te idaṁ’;
Taṁ dāni maṁ pabbajitaṁ samānaṁ,
Kiṅkāraṇā citta tuvaṁ na yuñjasi.
19.1.e:
For many years you begged me,
“Enough of living in a house for you!”
Why do you not urge me on, mind,
now that I’ve gone forth as an ascetic?

19.1.s:
Nanu ahaṁ citta tayāmhi yācito,
‘Giribbaje citrachadā vihaṅgamā’;
Mahindaghosatthanitābhigajjino,
Te taṁ ramessanti vanamhi jhāyinaṁ.
19.1.e:
Didn’t you entice me, mind:
“In the Mountainfold, the birds with colorful wings,
greeting the thunder, Mahinda’s voice,
will delight you as you meditate in the forest?”

19.1.s:
Kulamhi mitte ca piye ca ñātake,
Khiḍḍāratiṁ kāmaguṇañca loke;
Sabbaṁ pahāya imamajjhupāgato,
Athopi tvaṁ citta na mayha tussasi.

Mameva etaṁ na hi tvaṁ paresaṁ,
Sannāhakāle paridevitena kiṁ;
Sabbaṁ idaṁ calamiti pekkhamāno,
Abhinikkhamiṁ amatapadaṁ jigīsaṁ.
19.1.e:
This is mine alone, it doesn’t belong to others;
when it is time to don your armor, why lament?
Observing that all this is unstable,
I went forth, seeking the state free of death.

19.1.s:
Suyuttavādī dvipadānamuttamo,
Mahābhisakko naradammasārathi;
‘Cittaṁ calaṁ makkaṭasannibhaṁ iti,
Avītarāgena sudunnivārayaṁ’.
19.1.e:
He whose words are well-composed, <j>supreme among people,
great physician, <j>guide for those fit to train, said:
“The mind fidgets like a monkey,
so it’s very hard to control if you are not free of lust.”

19.1.s:
Kāmā hi citrā madhurā manoramā,
Aviddasū yattha sitā puthujjanā;
Te dukkhamicchanti punabbhavesino,
Cittena nītā niraye nirākatā.

‘Mayūrakoñcābhirutamhi kānane,
Dīpīhi byagghehi purakkhato vasaṁ;
Kāye apekkhaṁ jaha mā virādhaya’,
Itissu maṁ citta pure niyuñjasi.
19.1.e:
“Staying in the grove resounding with cries
of peacocks and herons, <j>and adorned by leopards and tigers,
abandon concern for the body, without fail!”
So you used to urge me, mind.

19.1.s:
‘Bhāvehi jhānāni ca indriyāni ca,
Balāni bojjhaṅgasamādhibhāvanā;
Tisso ca vijjā phusa buddhasāsane’,
Itissu maṁ citta pure niyuñjasi.
19.1.e:
“Develop the absorptions and spiritual faculties,
the powers, awakening factors, and immersion;
realize the three knowledges <j>in the teaching of the Buddha!”
So you used to urge me, mind.

19.1.s:
‘Bhāvehi maggaṁ amatassa pattiyā,
Niyyānikaṁ sabbadukhakkhayogadhaṁ;
Aṭṭhaṅgikaṁ sabbakilesasodhanaṁ’,
Itissu maṁ citta pure niyuñjasi.
19.1.e:
“Develop the eightfold path <j>to realize freedom from death
emancipating, its objective being <j>the end of all suffering,
and cleansing all defilements!”
So you used to urge me, mind.

19.1.s:
‘Dukkhanti khandhe paṭipassa yoniso,
Yato ca dukkhaṁ samudeti taṁ jaha;
Idheva dukkhassa karohi antaṁ’,
Itissu maṁ citta pure niyuñjasi.
19.1.e:
“Reflect rationally on the aggregates as suffering,
and abandon that from which suffering arises;
make an end of suffering in this very life!”
So you used to urge me, mind.

19.1.s:
‘Aniccaṁ dukkhanti vipassa yoniso,
Suññaṁ anattāti aghaṁ vadhanti ca;
Manovicāre uparundha cetaso’,
Itissu maṁ citta pure niyuñjasi.
19.1.e:
“Rationally discern that impermanence is suffering,
that emptiness is non-self, and that gloom is death.
Uproot the wandering mind!”
So you used to urge me, mind.

19.1.s:
‘Muṇḍo virūpo abhisāpamāgato,
Kapālahatthova kulesu bhikkhasu;
Yuñjassu satthuvacane mahesino’,
Itissu maṁ citta pure niyuñjasi.
19.1.e:
“Bald, unsightly, accursed,
seek alms amongst families, bowl in hand.
Devote yourself to the word of the Teacher, <j>the great seer!”
So you used to urge me, mind.

19.1.s:
‘Susaṁvutatto visikhantare caraṁ,
Kulesu kāmesu asaṅgamānaso;
Cando yathā dosinapuṇṇamāsiyā’,
Itissu maṁ citta pure niyuñjasi.
19.1.e:
“Wander among the street markets well-restrained,
mentally unchained to families and sensual pleasures,
like the full moon on a bright night!”
So you used to urge me, mind.

19.1.s:
‘Āraññiko hohi ca piṇḍapātiko,
Sosāniko hohi ca paṁsukūliko;
Nesajjiko hohi sadā dhute rato’,
Itissu maṁ citta pure niyuñjasi.
19.1.e:
“Be a wilderness-dweller and an alms-eater,
one who lives in charnel grounds, a rag-robe wearer,
one who never lies down, <j>always delighting in ascetic practices.”
So you used to urge me, mind.

19.1.s:
Ropetva rukkhāni yathā phalesī,
Mūle taruṁ chettu tameva icchasi;
Tathūpamaṁ cittamidaṁ karosi,
Yaṁ maṁ aniccamhi cale niyuñjasi.
19.1.e:
Mind, when you urge me to <j>the impermanent and unstable,
you’re acting like someone who plants trees,
then, when they’re about to fruit,
wishes to cut down the very same trees.

19.1.s:
Arūpa dūraṅgama ekacāri,
Na te karissaṁ vacanaṁ idānihaṁ;
Dukkhā hi kāmā kaṭukā mahabbhayā,
Nibbānamevābhimano carissaṁ.
19.1.e:
Incorporeal mind, far-traveler, lone-wanderer:
I won’t do your bidding any more.
Sensual pleasures are suffering, painful, <j>and very dangerous;
I’ll wander with my mind <j>focused only on extinguishment.

19.1.s:
Nāhaṁ alakkhyā ahirikkatāya vā,
Na cittahetū na ca dūrakantanā;
Ājīvahetū ca ahaṁ na nikkhamiṁ,
Kato ca te citta paṭissavo mayā.
19.1.e:
I didn’t go forth due to bad luck or shamelessness,
or due to a whim or banishment,
nor for the sake of a livelihood;
it was because I agreed <j>to the promise you made, mind.

19.1.s:
‘Appicchatā sappurisehi vaṇṇitā,
Makkhappahānaṁ vupasamo dukhassa’;
Itissu maṁ citta tadā niyuñjasi,
Idāni tvaṁ gacchasi pubbaciṇṇaṁ.
19.1.e:
“Having few wishes, abandoning disparagement,
the settling of suffering: <j>these are praised by true persons.”
So you used to urge me, mind,
but now you keep on with your old habits!

19.1.s:
Taṇhā avijjā ca piyāpiyañca,
Subhāni rūpāni sukhā ca vedanā;
Manāpiyā kāmaguṇā ca vantā,
Vante ahaṁ āvamituṁ na ussahe.
19.1.e:
Craving, ignorance, the loved and unloved,
pretty sights, pleasant feelings,
and the delightful kinds of sensual stimulation:
I’ve vomited them up, I can’t swallow them back.

19.1.s:
Sabbattha te citta vaco kataṁ mayā,
Bahūsu jātīsu na mesi kopito;
Ajjhattasambhavo kataññutāya te,
Dukkhe ciraṁ saṁsaritaṁ tayā kate.
19.1.e:
I’ve done your bidding everywhere, mind!
For many births, I’ve done nothing to upset you.
Yet the creation in myself <j>is because of your ingratitude—
for a long time I’ve transmigrated <j>in the suffering you’ve made.

19.1.s:
Tvaññeva no citta karosi brāhmaṇo,
Tvaṁ khattiyo rājadasī karosi;
Vessā ca suddā ca bhavāma ekadā,
Devattanaṁ vāpi taveva vāhasā.

Taveva hetū asurā bhavāmase,
Tvaṁmūlakaṁ nerayikā bhavāmase;
Atho tiracchānagatāpi ekadā,
Petattanaṁ vāpi taveva vāhasā.
19.1.e:
You alone make us titans;
because of you we’re born in hell.
Then sometimes we become animals,
and life as a ghost is also on account of you.

19.1.s:
Nanu dubbhissasi maṁ punappunaṁ,
Muhuṁ muhuṁ cāraṇikaṁva dassayaṁ;
Ummattakeneva mayā palobhasi,
Kiñcāpi te citta virādhitaṁ mayā.
19.1.e:
Come what may, you won’t betray me again,
dazzling me with your ever-changing display!
You play with me like I’m mad—
but how have I ever failed you, mind?

19.1.s:
Idaṁ pure cittamacāri cārikaṁ,
Yenicchakaṁ yatthakāmaṁ yathāsukhaṁ;
Tadajjahaṁ niggahessāmi yoniso,
Hatthippabhinnaṁ viya aṅkusaggaho.
19.1.e:
In the past my mind wandered
how it wished, where it liked, as it pleased.
Now I’ll carefully guide it,
as a trainer with a hook guides a rutting elephant.

19.1.s:
Satthā ca me lokamimaṁ adhiṭṭhahi,
Aniccato addhuvato asārato;
Pakkhanda maṁ citta jinassa sāsane,
Tārehi oghā mahatā suduttarā.
19.1.e:
The teacher willed that this world appear to me
as impermanent, unstable, insubstantial.
Mind, let me leap into the victor’s teaching,
carry me over the great flood, so hard to pass.

19.1.s:
Na te idaṁ citta yathā purāṇakaṁ,
Nāhaṁ alaṁ tuyha vase nivattituṁ;
Mahesino pabbajitomhi sāsane,
Na mādisā honti vināsadhārino.
19.1.e:
Things have changed, mind!
Nothing could make me return to your control!
I’ve gone forth in the teaching of the great seer,
those like me don’t come to ruin.

19.1.s:
Nagā samuddā saritā vasundharā,
Disā catasso vidisā adho divā;
Sabbe aniccā tibhavā upaddutā,
Kuhiṁ gato citta sukhaṁ ramissasi.

Dhitipparaṁ kiṁ mama citta kāhisi,
Na te alaṁ citta vasānuvattako;
Na jātu bhastaṁ ubhatomukhaṁ chupe,
Dhiratthu pūraṁ nava sotasandaniṁ.

Varāhaeṇeyyavigāḷhasevite,
Pabbhārakuṭṭe pakateva sundare;
Navambunā pāvusasitthakānane,
Tahiṁ guhāgehagato ramissasi.
19.1.e:
You’ve ascended the mountain peak, <j>full of nature’s beauty,
frequented by boars and antelopes,
a grove sprinkled with fresh water in the monsoon;
and there you’ll be happy in your cave-home.

19.1.s:
Sunīlagīvā susikhā supekhunā,
Sucittapattacchadanā vihaṅgamā;
Sumañjughosatthanitābhigajjino,
Te taṁ ramessanti vanamhi jhāyinaṁ.
19.1.e:
Peacocks with beautiful necks and crests,
colorful tail-feathers and wings,
crying out at the resounding thunder:
they’ll delight you as you meditate in the forest.

19.1.s:
Vuṭṭhamhi deve caturaṅgule tiṇe,
Sampupphite meghanibhamhi kānane;
Nagantare viṭapisamo sayissaṁ,
Taṁ me mudū hehiti tūlasannibhaṁ.
19.1.e:
When the heavens have rained, <j>and the grass is four inches high,
and the grove is full of flowers like a cloud,
between the mountains, like the fork of a tree, I’ll lie;
it will be as soft as cotton-buds.

19.1.s:
Tathā tu kassāmi yathāpi issaro,
Yaṁ labbhati tenapi hotu me alaṁ;
Na tāhaṁ kassāmi yathā atandito,
Biḷārabhastaṁva yathā sumadditaṁ.
19.1.e:
I’ll act rather as a master does:
let whatever I get be enough for me.
And that’s why I’ll make you as supple
as a tireless worker makes a cat-skin bag.

19.1.s:
Tathā tu kassāmi yathāpi issaro,
Yaṁ labbhati tenapi hotu me alaṁ;
Viriyena taṁ mayha vasānayissaṁ,
Gajaṁva mattaṁ kusalaṅkusaggaho.
19.1.e:
I’ll act rather as a master does:
let whatever I get be enough for me.
I’ll control you with my energy,
as a skilled trainer controls an elephant with a hook.

19.1.s:
Tayā sudantena avaṭṭhitena hi,
Hayena yoggācariyova ujjunā;
Pahomi maggaṁ paṭipajjituṁ sivaṁ,
Cittānurakkhīhi sadā nisevitaṁ.
19.1.e:
Now that you’re well-tamed and reliable,
I can use you, <j>like a trainer uses a straight-running horse,
to practice the path of grace,
cultivated by those who take care of their minds.

19.1.s:
Ārammaṇe taṁ balasā nibandhisaṁ,
Nāgaṁva thambhamhi daḷhāya rajjuyā;
Taṁ me suguttaṁ satiyā subhāvitaṁ,
Anissitaṁ sabbabhavesu hehisi.
19.1.e:
I shall strongly fasten you to a meditation subject,
as an elephant is tied to a post with firm rope.
You’ll be well-guarded by me, <j>well-developed by mindfulness,
and unattached to rebirth in all states of existence.

19.1.s:
Paññāya chetvā vipathānusārinaṁ,
Yogena niggayha pathe nivesiya;
Disvā samudayaṁ vibhavañca sambhavaṁ,
Dāyādako hehisi aggavādino.
19.1.e:
With wisdom you’ll cut short <j>the one following the wrong path,
curb them by meditation, <j>and settle them on the right path.
Having seen arising and passing away <j>with respect to the cause of suffering,
you’ll be an heir to the greatest teacher.

19.1.s:
Catubbipallāsavasaṁ adhiṭṭhitaṁ,
Gāmaṇḍalaṁva parinesi citta maṁ;
Nanu saṁyojanabandhanacchidaṁ,
Saṁsevase kāruṇikaṁ mahāmuniṁ.
19.1.e:
Under the sway of the four distortions, mind,
you dragged me around like a bull in a pit;
but now you won’t associate <j>with the great sage of compassion,
the cutter of fetters and bonds?

19.1.s:
Migo yathā seri sucittakānane,
Rammaṁ giriṁ pāvusaabbhamāliniṁ;
Anākule tattha nage ramissaṁ,
Asaṁsayaṁ citta parā bhavissasi.
19.1.e:
Like a deer roaming free in the colorful forest,
I’ll ascend the lovely mountain <j>wreathed in monsoon clouds,
and rejoice to be on that hill, free of folk—
there is no doubt you’ll perish, mind.

19.1.s:
Ye tuyha chandena vasena vattino,
Narā ca nārī ca anubhonti yaṁ sukhaṁ;
Aviddasū māravasānuvattino,
Bhavābhinandī tava citta sāvakā”ti.
19.1.e:
The men and women who live <j>under your will and command,
whatever pleasure they experience,
they are ignorant and fall under Māra’s control;
loving life, they’re your disciples, mind.

20.1.s:
“Āraññikā piṇḍapātikā,
uñchāpattāgate ratā;
Dālemu maccuno senaṁ,
ajjhattaṁ susamāhitā.
20.1.e:
“Living in the wilderness, eating only almsfood,
happy with the scraps in our bowls,
let us tear apart the army of death,
while remaining serene within.

20.1.s:
Āraññikā piṇḍapātikā,
uñchāpattāgate ratā;
Dhunāma maccuno senaṁ,
naḷāgāraṁva kuñjaro.
20.1.e:
Living in the wilderness, eating only almsfood,
happy with the scraps in our bowls,
let us crush the army of death,
as an elephant a hut of reeds.

20.1.s:
Rukkhamūlikā sātatikā,
uñchāpattāgate ratā;
Dālemu maccuno senaṁ,
ajjhattaṁ susamāhitā.
20.1.e:
Living at the foot of a tree, persistent,
happy with the scraps in our bowls,
let us tear apart the army of death,
while remaining serene within.

20.1.s:
Rukkhamūlikā sātatikā,
uñchāpattāgate ratā;
Dhunāma maccuno senaṁ,
naḷāgāraṁva kuñjaro”.
20.1.e:
Living at the foot of a tree, persistent,
happy with the scraps in our bowls,
let us crush the army of death,
as an elephant a hut of reeds.”

20.1.s:
“Aṭṭhikaṅkalakuṭike,
maṁsanhārupasibbite;
Dhiratthu pure duggandhe,
paragatte mamāyase.
20.1.e:
“You hut, made of a chain of bones,
sewn together with flesh and sinew;
curse you mortal frame, you stink,
you cherish the parts of others!

20.1.s:
Gūthabhaste taconaddhe,
uragaṇḍipisācini;
Nava sotāni te kāye,
yāni sandanti sabbadā.
20.1.e:
You sack of dung swathed in skin!
You demoness with horns on your chest!
O body, you have nine streams
that are flowing all the time.

20.1.s:
Tava sarīraṁ navasotaṁ,
Duggandhakaraṁ paribandhaṁ;
Bhikkhu parivajjayate taṁ,
Mīḷhaṁ ca yathā sucikāmo.
20.1.e:
With its nine streams,
your body stinks, full of dung.
A monk seeking purity
would avoid it like excrement.

20.1.s:
Evañce taṁ jano jaññā,
yathā jānāmi taṁ ahaṁ;
Ārakā parivajjeyya,
gūthaṭṭhānaṁva pāvuse”.
20.1.e:
If they knew you
like I do,
they’d keep far away,
like a cesspit in the monsoon.”

20.1.s:
“Evametaṁ mahāvīra,
yathā samaṇa bhāsasi;
Ettha ceke visīdanti,
paṅkamhiva jaraggavo”.
20.1.e:
“So it is, great hero!
As you say, ascetic!
But some founder here
like an old bull stuck in a bog.”

20.1.s:
“Ākāsamhi haliddiyā,
yo maññetha rajetave;
Aññena vāpi raṅgena,
vighātudayameva taṁ.
20.1.e:
“Whoever might think
of making the sky yellow,
or some other color,
would only trouble themselves.

20.1.s:
Tadākāsasamaṁ cittaṁ,
ajjhattaṁ susamāhitaṁ;
Mā pāpacitte āsādi,
aggikhandhaṁva pakkhimā”.
20.1.e:
This mind is like the sky:
serene inside itself.
Evil-minded one, don’t attack me,
you’ll end up like a moth in a mass of fire.”

20.1.s:
“Passa cittakataṁ bimbaṁ,
arukāyaṁ samussitaṁ;
Āturaṁ bahusaṅkappaṁ,
yassa natthi dhuvaṁ ṭhiti.
20.1.e:
“See this fancy puppet,
a body built of sores,
diseased, obsessed over,
in which nothing lasts at all.

20.1.s:
Passa cittakataṁ rūpaṁ,
maṇinā kuṇḍalena ca;
Aṭṭhiṁ tacena onaddhaṁ,
saha vatthehi sobhati.
20.1.e:
See this fancy figure,
with its gems and earrings;
it is bones swathed in skin,
made pretty by its clothes.

20.1.s:
Alattakakatā pādā,
mukhaṁ cuṇṇakamakkhitaṁ;
Alaṁ bālassa mohāya,
no ca pāragavesino.
20.1.e:
Rouged feet
and powdered face
may be enough to beguile a fool,
but not a seeker of the far shore.

20.1.s:
Aṭṭhapadakatā kesā,
nettā añjanamakkhitā;
Alaṁ bālassa mohāya,
no ca pāragavesino.
20.1.e:
Hair in eight braids
and eyeshadow
may be enough to beguile a fool,
but not a seeker of the far shore.

20.1.s:
Añjanīva navā cittā,
pūtikāyo alaṅkato;
Alaṁ bālassa mohāya,
no ca pāragavesino.
20.1.e:
A rotting body all adorned
like a freshly painted makeup box
may be enough to beguile a fool,
but not a seeker of the far shore.

20.1.s:
Odahi migavo pāsaṁ,
nāsadā vāguraṁ migo;
Bhutvā nivāpaṁ gacchāma,
kaddante migabandhake.
20.1.e:
The hunter laid his snare,
but the deer didn’t spring the trap.
I’ve eaten the bait and now I go,
leaving the trapper to lament.

20.1.s:
Chinno pāso migavassa,
nāsadā vāguraṁ migo;
Bhutvā nivāpaṁ gacchāma,
socante migaluddake”.
20.1.e:
The hunter’s snare is broken,
but the deer didn’t spring the trap.
I’ve eaten the bait and now I go,
leaving the deer-hunter to grieve.”

20.1.s:
“Tadāsi yaṁ bhiṁsanakaṁ,
tadāsi lomahaṁsanaṁ;
Anekākārasampanne,
sāriputtamhi nibbute.
20.1.e:
“Then there was terror!
Then they had goosebumps!
When Sāriputta, <j>endowed with many fine qualities,
became quenched.

20.1.s:
Aniccā vata saṅkhārā,
uppādavayadhammino;
Upajjitvā nirujjhanti,
tesaṁ vūpasamo sukho.

Sukhumaṁ te paṭivijjhanti,
vālaggaṁ usunā yathā;
Ye pañcakkhandhe passanti,
parato no ca attato.
20.1.e:
“Those who see the five aggregates
as other, not as self,
penetrate a subtle thing,
like a hair-tip with an arrow.

20.1.s:
Ye ca passanti saṅkhāre,
parato no ca attato;
Paccabyādhiṁsu nipuṇaṁ,
vālaggaṁ usunā yathā.
20.1.e:
Those who see conditions
as alien, not as self,
pierce a fine thing,
like a hair-tip with an arrow.”

20.1.s:
Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho,
ḍayhamānova matthake;
Kāmarāgappahānāya,
sato bhikkhu paribbaje.
20.1.e:
“Like they’re struck by a sword,
like their head was on fire,
a mendicant should wander mindful,
to give up sensual desire.

20.1.s:
Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho,
ḍayhamānova matthake;
Bhavarāgappahānāya,
sato bhikkhu paribbaje.
20.1.e:
Like they’re struck by a sword,
like their head was on fire,
a mendicant should wander mindful,
to give up desire for rebirth.”

20.1.s:
Codito bhāvitattena,
sarīrantimadhārinā;
Migāramātupāsādaṁ,
pādaṅguṭṭhena kampayiṁ.
20.1.e:
“Urged by the developed one,
who bore his final body,
I shook the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother
with my big toe.”

20.1.s:
Nayidaṁ sithilamārabbha,
nayidaṁ appena thāmasā;
Nibbānamadhigantabbaṁ,
sabbaganthapamocanaṁ.
20.1.e:
“Not by being slack,
or with little strength
may this be realized—extinguishment,
the release from all ties.”

20.1.s:
Ayañca daharo bhikkhu,
ayamuttamaporiso;
Dhāreti antimaṁ dehaṁ,
jetvā māraṁ savāhiniṁ.
20.1.e:
“This young monk,
this best of men,
bears his final body,
having vanquished Māra and his legions.”

20.1.s:
Vivaramanupabhanti vijjutā,
Vebhārassa ca paṇḍavassa ca;
Nagavivaragato jhāyati,
Putto appaṭimassa tādino.
20.1.e:
“Lightning flashes down
on the cleft of Vebhāra and Paṇḍava.
But in the mountain cleft he is absorbed in jhāna—
the son of the Buddha, inimitable and unaffected.”

20.1.s:
Upasanto uparato,
pantasenāsano muni;
Dāyādo buddhaseṭṭhassa,
brahmunā abhivandito”.
20.1.e:
“Calm and still,
the sage in his remote lodging,
the heir to the best of Buddhas,
is honored even by the Divinity.

20.1.s:
“Upasantaṁ uparataṁ,
pantasenāsanaṁ muniṁ;
Dāyādaṁ buddhaseṭṭhassa,
vanda brāhmaṇa kassapaṁ.
20.1.e:
Calm and still,
the sage in his remote lodging,
is heir to the best of Buddhas:
Brahmin, you should honor Kassapa!

20.1.s:
Yo ca jātisataṁ gacche,
sabbā brāhmaṇajātiyo;
Sottiyo vedasampanno,
manussesu punappunaṁ.
20.1.e:
Even if someone were to be born again and again
a hundred times in the human realm,
and always as a brahmin,
a student accomplished in the Vedas;

20.1.s:
Ajjhāyakopi ce assa,
tiṇṇaṁ vedāna pāragū;
Etassa vandanāyetaṁ,
kalaṁ nāgghati soḷasiṁ.
20.1.e:
and if he were to become a reciter,
a master of the three Vedas:
honoring such a person
isn’t worth a sixteenth of that.

20.1.s:
Yo so aṭṭha vimokkhāni,
purebhattaṁ aphassayi;
Anulomaṁ paṭilomaṁ,
tato piṇḍāya gacchati.
20.1.e:
One who attains the eight liberations
forwards and backwards
before breakfast,
and then goes on almsround—

don’t attack such a mendicant!
Don’t ruin yourself, brahmin!
Let your heart have trust
in the perfected one, the unaffected;
quickly venerate him with cupped palms:
don’t let your head explode!”

20.1.s:
“Neso passati saddhammaṁ,
saṁsārena purakkhato;
Adhogamaṁ jimhapathaṁ,
kummaggamanudhāvati.
20.1.e:
“If you prioritize transmigration,
you don’t see the true teaching.
You’re following a twisted path,
a bad path that will lead you down.

20.1.s:
Kimīva mīḷhasallitto,
saṅkhāre adhimucchito;
Pagāḷho lābhasakkāre,
tuccho gacchati poṭṭhilo”.
20.1.e:
Like a worm smeared with dung,
he is besotted with conditions.
Consumed by gain and honor,
Poṭṭhila goes on, hollow.”

20.1.s:
“Imañca passa āyantaṁ,
sāriputtaṁ sudassanaṁ;
Vimuttaṁ ubhatobhāge,
ajjhattaṁ susamāhitaṁ.

Visallaṁ khīṇasaṁyogaṁ,
tevijjaṁ maccuhāyinaṁ;
Dakkhiṇeyyaṁ manussānaṁ,
puññakkhettaṁ anuttaraṁ”.
20.1.e:
free of thorns, with yoking ended,
master of the three knowledges, <j>conqueror of death;
worthy of offerings,
a supreme field of merit for the people.”

“These many gods,
powerful and glorious,
all 10,000 of them,
are priests of Divinity.
They stand with cupped palms
honoring Moggallāna:

20.1.s:
‘Namo te purisājañña,
namo te purisuttama;
Yassa te āsavā khīṇā,
dakkhiṇeyyosi mārisa’.
20.1.e:
‘Homage to you, O thoroughbred!
Homage to you, supreme among men!
Since your defilements are ended,
you, good fellow, are worthy of teacher’s offerings.’

20.1.s:
Pūjito naradevena,
uppanno maraṇābhibhū;
Puṇḍarīkaṁva toyena,
saṅkhārenupalippati.
20.1.e:
Venerated by the lordly god,
he has arisen, the master of death.
He is unsmeared by conditions,
as a lotus-flower by water.”

20.1.s:
Yassa muhuttena sahassadhā loko,
Saṁvidito sabrahmakappo vasi;
Iddhiguṇe cutupapāte kāle,
Passati devatā sa bhikkhu”.
20.1.e:
“The mendicant by whom the galaxy
with the age of the Divinity are known in an hour—
that master of psychic ability sees the gods
at the time they pass away and are reborn.”

20.1.s:
“Sāriputtova paññāya,
sīlena upasamena ca;
Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu,
etāvaparamo siyā.
20.1.e:
“Sāriputta is full of wisdom,
ethics, and peace.
Even a mendicant who has crossed over
might at best equal him.

20.1.s:
Koṭisatasahassassa,
Attabhāvaṁ khaṇena nimmine;
Ahaṁ vikubbanāsu kusalo,
Vasībhūtomhi iddhiyā.
20.1.e:
But in a moment I can create the likenesses
of ten million times 100,000 people!
I’m skilled in transformations;
I’m a master of psychic powers.

20.1.s:
Samādhivijjāvasipāramīgato,
Moggallānagotto asitassa sāsane;
Dhīro samucchindi samāhitindriyo,
Nāgo yathā pūtilataṁva bandhanaṁ.
20.1.e:
A member of the Moggallāna clan, <j>attained to perfection and mastery
in immersion and knowledge, <j>wise in the teachings of the unattached,
with serene faculties, has burst his bonds
like an elephant bursts a vine.

20.1.s:
Pariciṇṇo mayā satthā,
kataṁ buddhassa sāsanaṁ;
Ohito garuko bhāro,
bhavanetti samūhatā.
20.1.e:
I’ve served the Teacher
and fulfilled the Buddha’s instructions.
The heavy burden is laid down,
the leash to existence is eradicated.

20.1.s:
Yassa catthāya pabbajito,
agārasmānagāriyaṁ;
So me attho anuppatto,
sabbasaṁyojanakkhayo.
20.1.e:
I’ve attained the goal
for the sake of which I went forth
from the lay life to homelessness—
the ending of all fetters.”

20.1.s:
Kīdiso nirayo āsi,
yattha dussī apaccatha;
Vidhuraṁ sāvakamāsajja,
kakusandhañca brāhmaṇaṁ.
20.1.e:
“What kind of hell was that,
where Dūsī was roasted
after attacking the disciple Vidhura
along with the brahmin Kakusandha?

There were 100 iron spikes,
each one uniquely painful.
That’s the kind of hell
where Dūsī was roasted
after attacking the disciple Vidhura
along with the brahmin Kakusandha.

20.1.s:
Yo etamabhijānāti,
bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;
Tādisaṁ bhikkhumāsajja,
kaṇha dukkhaṁ nigacchasi.
20.1.e:
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.

There are mansions that last an eon
standing in the middle of a lake.
Sapphire-colored, brilliant,
they sparkle and shine.
Dancing there are nymphs
shining in all different colors.

20.1.s:
Yo etamabhijānāti,
… pe
…
kaṇha dukkhaṁ nigacchasi.
20.1.e:
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.

20.1.s:
Yo ve buddhena codito,
bhikkhusaṅghassa pekkhato;
Migāramātupāsādaṁ,
pādaṅguṭṭhena kampayi.
20.1.e:
I’m the one who, urged by the Buddha,
shook the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother
with his big toe
as the Saṅgha of mendicants watched.

20.1.s:
Yo etamabhijānāti,
… pe
…
kaṇha dukkhaṁ nigacchasi.
20.1.e:
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.

20.1.s:
Yo vejayantapāsādaṁ,
pādaṅguṭṭhena kampayi;
Iddhibalenupatthaddho,
saṁvejesi ca devatā.
20.1.e:
I’m the one who shook the Palace of Victory
with his big toe
owing to psychic power,
inspiring deities to awe.

20.1.s:
Yo etamabhijānāti,
… pe
…
kaṇha dukkhaṁ nigacchasi.
20.1.e:
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.

I’m the one who asked Sakka
in the Palace of Victory:
‘Respectable sir, I hope you recall
the one who is freed through the ending of craving?’
And I’m the one to whom Sakka
admitted the truth when asked.

20.1.s:
“Yo etamabhijānāti,
… pe
…
kaṇha dukkhaṁ nigacchasi.
20.1.e:
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.

I’m the one who asked the Divinity
in the Hall of Clear Right before the assembly:
‘Respectable sir, do you still have the same view
that you had in the past?
Or do you see the radiance
surpassing the realm of divinity?’

20.1.s:
Tassa brahmā viyākāsi,
pañhaṁ puṭṭho yathātathaṁ;
Na me mārisa sā diṭṭhi,
yā me diṭṭhi pure ahu.
20.1.e:
And I’m the one to whom the Divinity
admitted the truth when asked.
‘Good fellow, I don’t have that view
that I had in the past.

20.1.s:
Passāmi vītivattantaṁ,
brahmaloke pabhassaraṁ;
Sohaṁ ajja kathaṁ vajjaṁ,
ahaṁ niccomhi sassato”.
20.1.e:
I see the radiance
surpassing the realm of divinity.
So how could I say today
that I am permanent and eternal?’

20.1.s:
“Yo etamabhijānāti,
… pe
…
kaṇha dukkhaṁ nigacchasi.
20.1.e:
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.

20.1.s:
Yo mahāneruno kūṭaṁ,
vimokkhena aphassayi;
Vanaṁ pubbavidehānaṁ,
ye ca bhūmisayā narā.
20.1.e:
I’m the one who touched the peak of Mount Neru
using the power of meditative liberation.
I’ve visited the forests of the people
who dwell in the land east of Videha.

20.1.s:
Yo etamabhijānāti,
bhikkhu buddhassa sāvako;
Tādisaṁ bhikkhumāsajja,
kaṇha dukkhaṁ nigacchasi.
20.1.e:
Dark One, if you attack
a mendicant who directly knows this,
a disciple of the Buddha,
you’ll fall into suffering.

20.1.s:
Na ve aggi cetayati,
ahaṁ bālaṁ ḍahāmīti;
Bālova jalitaṁ aggiṁ,
āsajja naṁ paḍayhati.
20.1.e:
Though a fire doesn’t think,
‘I’ll burn the fool!’
Still the fool who attacks
the fire gets burnt.

20.1.s:
Evamevaṁ tuvaṁ māra,
āsajja naṁ tathāgataṁ;
Sayaṁ ḍahissasi attānaṁ,
bālo aggiṁva samphusaṁ.
20.1.e:
In the same way, Māra,
in attacking the Realized One,
you’ll only burn yourself,
like a fool touching the flames.

20.1.s:
Apuññaṁ pasavī māro,
āsajja naṁ tathāgataṁ;
Kiṁ nu maññasi pāpima,
na me pāpaṁ vipaccati.
20.1.e:
Māra’s done a bad thing
in attacking the Realized One.
Wicked One, do you imagine that
your wickedness won’t bear fruit?

20.1.s:
Karato te cīyate pāpaṁ,
cirarattāya antaka;
Māra nibbinda buddhamhā,
āsaṁ mākāsi bhikkhusu”.
20.1.e:
Your deeds heap up wickedness
that will last a long time, terminator!
Give up on the Buddha, Māra!
And hold no hope for the mendicants!”

20.1.s:
“Iti māraṁ atajjesi,
bhikkhu bhesakaḷāvane;
Tato so dummano yakkho,
tatthevantaradhāyathā”ti.
20.1.e:
That is how, in the Bhesekaḷā grove,
the mendicant warned Māra.
That spirit, downcast,
disappeared right there.

21.1.s:
“Nikkhantaṁ vata maṁ santaṁ,
agārasmānagāriyaṁ;
Vitakkā upadhāvanti,
pagabbhā kaṇhato ime.
21.1.e:
“Now that I’ve renounced
the lay life for homelessness,
I’m overrun
by the rude thoughts of the Dark One.

21.1.s:
Uggaputtā mahissāsā,
sikkhitā daḷhadhammino;
Samantā parikireyyuṁ,
sahassaṁ apalāyinaṁ.
21.1.e:
Even if a thousand warrior chiefs and great archers,
well trained, with strong bows,
were to completely surround me;
I would never flee.

21.1.s:
Sacepi ettakā bhiyyo,
āgamissanti itthiyo;
Neva maṁ byādhayissanti,
dhamme samhi patiṭṭhito.
21.1.e:
And even if women come,
many more than that,
they won’t bother me,
for I stand firm in the teaching.

21.1.s:
Sakkhī hi me sutaṁ etaṁ,
buddhassādiccabandhuno;
Nibbānagamanaṁ maggaṁ,
tattha me nirato mano.

Evañce maṁ viharantaṁ,
pāpima upagacchasi;
Tathā maccu karissāmi,
na me maggampi dakkhasi.
21.1.e:
Wicked One, if you come near me
as I meditate like this,
I’ll make sure that you, Death,
won’t even see the path I take.”

21.1.s:
Aratiñca ratiñca pahāya,
Sabbaso gehasitañca vitakkaṁ;
Vanathaṁ na kareyya kuhiñci,
Nibbanatho avanatho sa bhikkhu.
21.1.e:
“Giving up desire and discontent,
along with all thought of domestic life,
they wouldn’t get snarled in anything;
unsnarled, free of snarls: that’s a real mendicant.

21.1.s:
Yamidha pathaviñca vehāsaṁ,
Rūpagataṁ jagatogadhaṁ kiñci;
Parijīyati sabbamaniccaṁ,
Evaṁ samecca caranti mutattā.
21.1.e:
Whatever here is included in form—
on earth, in the sky, or in planet’s deep—
wears out, it is all impermanent:
the self-examined live having comprehended this.

21.1.s:
Upadhīsu janā gadhitāse,
Diṭṭhasute paṭighe ca mute ca;
Ettha vinodaya chandamanejo,
Yo hettha na limpati muni tamāhu.
21.1.e:
People are bound to their attachments,
to impingement of the seen and heard, <j>and to what is thought.
Unstirred, dispel desire for these things;
for one called ‘a sage’ does not cling to them.

21.1.s:
Atha saṭṭhisitā savitakkā,
Puthujjanatāya adhammā niviṭṭhā;
Na ca vaggagatassa kuhiñci,
No pana duṭṭhullagāhī sa bhikkhu.
21.1.e:
Trapped in the sixty wrong views, <j>full of their own opinions,
ordinary people are fixed in wrong principles.
But that mendicant wouldn’t join a sect,
still less would they utter lewd speech.

21.1.s:
Dabbo cirarattasamāhito,
Akuhako nipako apihālu;
Santaṁ padaṁ ajjhagamā muni,
Paṭicca parinibbuto kaṅkhati kālaṁ.
21.1.e:
Proficient, long serene,
free of deceit, alert, without envy,
the sage has reached the state of peace;
quenched, he awaits his time.”

21.1.s:
Mānaṁ pajahassu gotama,
Mānapathañca jahassu asesaṁ;
Mānapathamhi sa mucchito,
Vippaṭisārīhuvā cirarattaṁ.
21.1.e:
“Give up conceit, Gotama!
Completely abandon the different kinds of conceit!
Besotted with the different kinds of conceit,
you’ve had regrets for a long time.

21.1.s:
Makkhena makkhitā pajā,
Mānahatā nirayaṁ papatanti;
Socanti janā cirarattaṁ,
Mānahatā nirayaṁ upapannā.
21.1.e:
Smeared by smears and slain by conceit,
people fall into hell.
When people slain by conceit are reborn in hell,
they grieve for a long time.

21.1.s:
Na hi socati bhikkhu kadāci,
Maggajino sammā paṭipanno;
Kittiñca sukhañcānubhoti,
Dhammadasoti tamāhu tathattaṁ.
21.1.e:
But a mendicant who practices rightly,
a path-victor, never grieves.
They enjoy happiness and a good reputation,
and they rightly call him a ‘Seer of Truth’.

21.1.s:
Tasmā akhilo idha padhānavā,
Nīvaraṇāni pahāya visuddho;
Mānañca pahāya asesaṁ,
Vijjāyantakaro samitāvī”.
21.1.e:
So being not hard-hearted, but energetic,
with hindrances given up, pure;
and having completely given up conceit,
the one who makes an end with knowledge <j>is assuaged.”

21.1.s:
“Kāmarāgena ḍayhāmi,
cittaṁ me pariḍayhati;
Sādhu nibbāpanaṁ brūhi,
anukampāya gotama”.
21.1.e:
“I’ve got a burning desire for pleasure;
my mind is on fire!
Please, out of compassion, Gotama,
tell me how to quench the flames.”

21.1.s:
“Saññāya vipariyesā,
cittaṁ te pariḍayhati;
Nimittaṁ parivajjehi,
subhaṁ rāgūpasaṁhitaṁ. (…)
21.1.e:
“Your mind is on fire
because of a perversion of perception.
Turn away from the sign
that’s attractive, provoking lust.

21.1.s:
Asubhāya cittaṁ bhāvehi,
ekaggaṁ susamāhitaṁ;
Sati kāyagatā tyatthu,
nibbidābahulo bhava.
21.1.e:
With your mind unified and serene,
meditate on the ugly aspects of the body.
With mindfulness immersed in the body,
be full of disillusionment.

21.1.s:
Animittañca bhāvehi,
mānānusayamujjaha;
Tato mānābhisamayā,
upasanto carissasi”.
21.1.e:
Meditate on the signless,
give up the tendency to conceit;
and when you comprehend conceit,
you will live at peace.”

21.1.s:
“Tameva vācaṁ bhāseyya,
yāyattānaṁ na tāpaye;
Pare ca na vihiṁseyya,
sā ve vācā subhāsitā.
21.1.e:
“Speak only those words
that do not hurt yourself
nor harm others;
such speech is truly well spoken.

21.1.s:
Piyavācameva bhāseyya,
yā vācā paṭinanditā;
Yaṁ anādāya pāpāni,
paresaṁ bhāsate piyaṁ.
21.1.e:
Speak only pleasing words,
words gladly welcomed.
Pleasing words are those
that bring nothing bad to others.

21.1.s:
Saccaṁ ve amatā vācā,
esa dhammo sanantano;
Sacce atthe ca dhamme ca,
āhu santo patiṭṭhitā.
21.1.e:
Truth itself is undying speech:
this is an ancient teaching.
Good people say the teaching and meaning
are grounded in truth.

21.1.s:
Yaṁ buddho bhāsati vācaṁ,
khemaṁ nibbānapattiyā;
Dukkhassantakiriyāya,
sā ve vācānamuttamā”.

“Gambhīrapañño medhāvī,
maggāmaggassa kovido;
Sāriputto mahāpañño,
dhammaṁ deseti bhikkhunaṁ.
21.1.e:
“Deep in wisdom, intelligent,
expert in the path and what is not the path;
Sāriputta, so greatly wise,
teaches Dhamma to the mendicants.

21.1.s:
Saṅkhittenapi deseti,
vitthārenapi bhāsati;
Sālikāyiva nigghoso,
paṭibhānaṁ udiyyati.
21.1.e:
He teaches in brief,
or he speaks at length.
His call, like a myna bird,
overflows with inspiration.

While he teaches
the mendicants listen to his sweet voice,
sounding attractive,
clear and graceful.
They listen joyfully,
their hearts elated.”

21.1.s:
“Ajja pannarase visuddhiyā,
Bhikkhū pañcasatā samāgatā;
Saṁyojanabandhanacchidā,
Anīghā khīṇapunabbhavā isī.
21.1.e:
“Today, on the fifteenth day sabbath,
five hundred monks have gathered together <j>to purify their precepts.
These untroubled sages <j>have cut off their fetters and bonds,
they will not be reborn again.

21.1.s:
Cakkavattī yathā rājā,
amaccaparivārito;
Samantā anupariyeti,
sāgarantaṁ mahiṁ imaṁ.
21.1.e:
Just as a wheel-rolling monarch
surrounded by ministers
travels all around this
land that’s girt by sea.

21.1.s:
Evaṁ vijitasaṅgāmaṁ,
satthavāhaṁ anuttaraṁ;
Sāvakā payirupāsanti,
tevijjā maccuhāyino.
21.1.e:
So disciples with the three knowledges,
conquerors of death,
revere the winner of the battle,
the unsurpassed caravan leader.

21.1.s:
Sabbe bhagavato puttā,
palāpettha na vijjati;
Taṇhāsallassa hantāraṁ,
vande ādiccabandhunaṁ.
21.1.e:
All are sons of the Blessed One—
there is no rubbish here.
I bow to the Kinsman of the Sun,
destroyer of the dart of craving.”

21.1.s:
Parosahassaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ,
sugataṁ payirupāsati;
Desentaṁ virajaṁ dhammaṁ,
nibbānaṁ akutobhayaṁ.
21.1.e:
“Over a thousand mendicants
revere the Holy One
as he teaches the immaculate Dhamma,
extinguishment, fearing nothing from any quarter.

21.1.s:
Suṇanti dhammaṁ vimalaṁ,
sammāsambuddhadesitaṁ;
Sobhati vata sambuddho,
bhikkhusaṅghapurakkhato.
21.1.e:
They listen to the immaculate Dhamma
taught by the fully awakened Buddha;
the Buddha shines
at the fore of the mendicant Saṅgha.

21.1.s:
‘Nāganāmo’si bhagavā,
isīnaṁ isisattamo;
Mahāmeghova hutvāna,
sāvake abhivassasi.
21.1.e:
Blessed One, your name is ‘Giant’,
seventh of the seers.
You are like a great cloud
that rains on your disciples.

21.1.s:
Divā vihārā nikkhamma,
satthudassanakamyatā;
Sāvako te mahāvīra,
pāde vandati vaṅgiso”.
21.1.e:
I’ve left my day’s meditation,
out of desire to see the Teacher.
Great hero, your disciple Vaṅgīsa
bows at your feet.”

21.1.s:
“Ummaggapathaṁ mārassa,
Abhibhuyya carati pabhijja khīlāni;
Taṁ passatha bandhapamuñcakaraṁ,
Asitaṁva bhāgaso pavibhajja.
21.1.e:
“Having overcome Māra’s wrong path,
you wander with hard-heartedness dissolved.
See him, the liberator from bonds,
dissecting the unattached section by section.

21.1.s:
Oghassa hi nitaraṇatthaṁ,
Anekavihitaṁ maggaṁ akkhāsi;
Tasmiñca amate akkhāte,
Dhammadasā ṭhitā asaṁhīrā.
21.1.e:
You have explained in many ways
the path to cross the flood.
The Seers of Truth stand unfaltering
in the freedom from death explained by you.

21.1.s:
Pajjotakaro ativijjha,
Sabbaṭhitīnaṁ atikkamamaddasa;
Ñatvā ca sacchikatvā ca,
Aggaṁ so desayi dasaddhānaṁ.
21.1.e:
As the bringer of light who has pierced the truth,
you’ve seen what lies beyond all planes.
When you saw and realized this for yourself,
you taught it first to the group of five.

21.1.s:
Evaṁ sudesite dhamme,
Ko pamādo vijānataṁ dhammaṁ;
Tasmā hi tassa bhagavato sāsane,
Appamatto sadā namassamanusikkhe”.
21.1.e:
When the Dhamma has been so well taught,
how could those who know it be negligent?
That’s why, being diligent, we should always train
respectfully in the Buddha’s teaching.”

21.1.s:
“Buddhānubuddho yo thero,
koṇḍañño tibbanikkamo;
Lābhī sukhavihārānaṁ,
vivekānaṁ abhiṇhaso.
21.1.e:
“The senior monk awakened after the Buddha,
Koṇḍañña, is keenly energetic.
He regularly gains
the blissful meditations of seclusion.

21.1.s:
Yaṁ sāvakena pattabbaṁ,
satthu sāsanakārinā;
Sabbassa taṁ anuppattaṁ,
appamattassa sikkhato.
21.1.e:
Whatever can be attained by a disciple
who does the Teacher’s bidding,
he has attained it all,
through diligently training himself.

21.1.s:
Mahānubhāvo tevijjo,
cetopariyakovido;
Koṇḍañño buddhadāyādo,
pāde vandati satthuno”.
21.1.e:
With great power and the three knowledges,
expert in encompassing the minds of others,
Koṇḍañña, the heir to the Buddha,
bows at the Teacher’s feet.”

21.1.s:
“Nagassa passe āsīnaṁ,
muniṁ dukkhassa pāraguṁ;
Sāvakā payirupāsanti,
tevijjā maccuhāyino.
21.1.e:
“As the sage, who has gone beyond suffering,
sits upon the mountain slope,
he is revered by disciples with the three knowledges,
conquerors of death.

21.1.s:
Cetasā anupariyeti,
moggallāno mahiddhiko;
Cittaṁ nesaṁ samanvesaṁ,
vippamuttaṁ nirūpadhiṁ.
21.1.e:
Moggallāna, of great psychic power,
encompasses with his mind,
scrutinizing their minds,
liberated, free of attachments.

21.1.s:
Evaṁ sabbaṅgasampannaṁ,
muniṁ dukkhassa pāraguṁ;
Anekākārasampannaṁ,
payirupāsanti gotamaṁ”.
21.1.e:
That is how those endowed <j>with many fine qualities
revere Gotama,
the sage gone beyond suffering,
perfect in every respect.”

21.1.s:
“Cando yathā vigatavalāhake nabhe,
Virocati vītamalova bhāṇumā;
Evampi aṅgīrasa tvaṁ mahāmuni,
Atirocasi yasasā sabbalokaṁ”.
21.1.e:
“Like the moon on a cloudless night,
like the shining immaculate sun,
so too Aṅgīrasa, O great sage,
your glory outshines the entire world.”

21.1.s:
“Kāveyyamattā vicarimha pubbe,
Gāmā gāmaṁ purā puraṁ;
Athaddasāma sambuddhaṁ,
Sabbadhammāna pāraguṁ.
21.1.e:
“We used to wander, drunk on poetry,
from village to village, town to town.
Then we saw the Buddha,
who has gone beyond all things.

21.1.s:
So me dhammamadesesi,
muni dukkhassa pāragū;
Dhammaṁ sutvā pasīdimha,
saddhā no udapajjatha.
21.1.e:
He, the sage gone beyond suffering,
taught me the Dhamma.
When we heard the Dhamma, <j>we became confident—
faith arose in us.

21.1.s:
Tassāhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,
khandhe āyatanāni ca;
Dhātuyo ca viditvāna,
pabbajiṁ anagāriyaṁ.
21.1.e:
Hearing him speak of
the aggregates, the sense-fields,
and the elements, I understood;
and then I went forth to homelessness.

21.1.s:
Bahūnaṁ vata atthāya,
uppajjanti tathāgatā;
Itthīnaṁ purisānañca,
ye te sāsanakārakā.
21.1.e:
It is for the benefit of many
that the Realized Ones arise—
the men and women
who follow their instructions.

21.1.s:
Tesaṁ kho vata atthāya,
bodhimajjhagamā muni;
Bhikkhūnaṁ bhikkhunīnañca,
ye nirāmagataddasā.
21.1.e:
It is truly for their benefit
that the sage realized awakening—
for the monks and for the nuns
who see that they’ve reached certainty.

21.1.s:
Sudesitā cakkhumatā,
buddhenādiccabandhunā;
Cattāri ariyasaccāni,
anukampāya pāṇinaṁ.
21.1.e:
The Clear-eyed One, the Buddha,
the Kinsman of the Sun,
has well taught the four noble truths
out of sympathy for living creatures.

21.1.s:
Dukkhaṁ dukkhasamuppādaṁ,
Dukkhassa ca atikkamaṁ;
Ariyaṁ caṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ,
Dukkhūpasamagāminaṁ.
21.1.e:
Suffering, suffering’s origin,
suffering’s transcendence,
and the noble eightfold path
that leads to the stilling of suffering.

21.1.s:
Evamete tathā vuttā,
diṭṭhā me te yathā tathā;
Sadattho me anuppatto,
kataṁ buddhassa sāsanaṁ.
21.1.e:
As these things were taught,
so I have seen them.
I’ve realized my heart’s goal,
and fulfilled the Buddha’s instructions.

21.1.s:
Svāgataṁ vata me āsi,
mama buddhassa santike;
Suvibhattesu dhammesu,
yaṁ seṭṭhaṁ tadupāgamiṁ.
21.1.e:
It was so welcome for me
to be in the presence of the Buddha.
Of the well-explained teachings,
I arrived at the best.

21.1.s:
Abhiññāpāramippatto,
sotadhātu visodhitā;
Tevijjo iddhipattomhi,
cetopariyakovido”.

“Pucchāmi satthāramanomapaññaṁ,
Diṭṭheva dhamme yo vicikicchānaṁ chettā;
Aggāḷave kālamakāsi bhikkhu,
Ñāto yasassī abhinibbutatto.
21.1.e:
“I ask the Teacher unrivaled in wisdom,
who has cut off all doubts in this very life:
a monk has died at Āḷavī’s premier shrine,
who was well-known, famous, and quenched.

21.1.s:
Nigrodhakappo iti tassa nāmaṁ,
Tayā kataṁ bhagavā brāhmaṇassa;
So taṁ namassaṁ acari mutyapekho,
Āraddhavīriyo daḷhadhammadassī.
21.1.e:
Nigrodhakappa was his name;
it was given to that brahmin by you, Blessed One.
He wandered in your honor, yearning for freedom,
energetic, a resolute Seer of Truth.

21.1.s:
Taṁ sāvakaṁ sakka mayampi sabbe,
Aññātumicchāma samantacakkhu;
Samavaṭṭhitā no savanāya sotā,
Tuvaṁ no satthā tvamanuttarosi.
21.1.e:
O Sakyan, All-seer,
we all wish to know about that disciple.
Our ears are eager to hear,
for you are the most excellent teacher.

21.1.s:
Chinda no vicikicchaṁ brūhi metaṁ,
Parinibbutaṁ vedaya bhūripañña;
Majjheva no bhāsa samantacakkhu,
Sakkova devāna sahassanetto.
21.1.e:
Cut off our doubt, declare this to us;
your wisdom is vast, tell us of his quenching!
All-seer, speak among us,
like the thousand-eyed Sakka <j>in the midst of the gods!

21.1.s:
Ye keci ganthā idha mohamaggā,
Aññāṇapakkhā vicikicchaṭhānā;
Tathāgataṁ patvā na te bhavanti,
Cakkhuñhi etaṁ paramaṁ narānaṁ.
21.1.e:
Whatever ties there are, or paths to delusion,
or things on the side of unknowing, <j>or that are bases of doubt
vanish on reaching a Realized One,
for his eye is the best of all people’s.

21.1.s:
No ce hi jātu puriso kilese,
Vāto yathā abbhaghanaṁ vihāne;
Tamovassa nivuto sabbaloko,
Jotimantopi na pabhāseyyuṁ.
21.1.e:
If no man were ever to disperse corruptions,
like the wind dispersing the stormclouds,
darkness would shroud the whole world;
not even brilliant men would shine.

21.1.s:
Dhīrā ca pajjotakarā bhavanti,
Taṁ taṁ ahaṁ vīra tatheva maññe;
Vipassinaṁ jānamupāgamimha,
Parisāsu no āvikarohi kappaṁ.
21.1.e:
The attentive are bringers of light;
my hero, that is what I think of you.
We’ve come for your discernment and knowledge:
here in this assembly, declare to us about Kappāyana.

21.1.s:
Khippaṁ giraṁ eraya vaggu vagguṁ,
Haṁsova paggayha saṇikaṁ nikūja;
Bindussarena suvikappitena,
Sabbeva te ujjugatā suṇoma.
21.1.e:
Swiftly send forth your sweet, sweet voice,
like a goose stretching its neck, gently honking,
lucid-flowing, with lovely tone:
alert, we all listen to you.

21.1.s:
Pahīnajātimaraṇaṁ asesaṁ,
Niggayha dhonaṁ vadessāmi dhammaṁ;
Na kāmakāro hi puthujjanānaṁ,
Saṅkheyyakāro ca tathāgatānaṁ.
21.1.e:
You have entirely abandoned birth and death;
curbed and pure, I urge you, speak the Dhamma!
For ordinary people <j>have no wish-granter,
but Realized Ones <j>have a comprehensibility-granter.

21.1.s:
Sampannaveyyākaraṇaṁ tavedaṁ,
Samujjupaññassa samuggahītaṁ;
Ayamañjali pacchimo suppaṇāmito,
Mā mohayī jānamanomapañña.
21.1.e:
Your answer is definitive, and we will adopt it,
for you have perfect understanding.
We raise our cupped palms one last time,
one of unrivaled wisdom, <j>don’t deliberately confuse us.

21.1.s:
Paroparaṁ ariyadhammaṁ viditvā,
Mā mohayī jānamanomavīriya;
Vāriṁ yathā ghammani ghammatatto,
Vācābhikaṅkhāmi sutaṁ pavassa.
21.1.e:
Knowing the teaching of the noble ones <j>from top to bottom,
one of unrivaled energy, <j>don’t deliberately confuse us.
Like a man baking in the summer sun <j>would long for water,
I long for your voice, so let the sound rain forth.

21.1.s:
Yadatthikaṁ brahmacariyaṁ acarī,
Kappāyano kaccissataṁ amoghaṁ;
Nibbāyi so ādu saupādiseso,
Yathā vimutto ahu taṁ suṇoma”.
21.1.e:
Surely Kappāyana did not <j>lead the spiritual life in vain?
Did he realize quenching,
or did he still have a residue?
Let us hear what kind of liberation he had!”

21.1.s:
“Acchecchi taṇhaṁ idha nāmarūpe, (iti bhagavā)
Kaṇhassa sotaṁ dīgharattānusayitaṁ;
Atāri jātiṁ maraṇaṁ asesaṁ,
Iccabravi bhagavā pañcaseṭṭho”.
21.1.e:
“He cut off craving for name and form right here,” said the Buddha,
“the river of darkness that had long lain within him.
He has entirely crossed over birth and death.”
So declared the Blessed One, the leader of the five.

21.1.s:
“Esa sutvā pasīdāmi,
vaco te isisattama;
Amoghaṁ kira me puṭṭhaṁ,
na maṁ vañcesi brāhmaṇo.
21.1.e:
“Now that I have heard your words,
seventh of seers, I am confident.
My question, it seems, was not in vain,
the brahmin did not deceive me.

21.1.s:
Yathā vādī tathā kārī,
ahu buddhassa sāvako;
Acchecchi maccuno jālaṁ,
tataṁ māyāvino daḷhaṁ.
21.1.e:
As he said, so he did—
he was a disciple of the Buddha.
He cut the net of death the deceiver,
so extended and strong.

21.1.s:
Addasa bhagavā ādiṁ,
upādānassa kappiyo;
Accagā vata kappāno,
maccudheyyaṁ suduttaraṁ.
21.1.e:
Blessed One, Kappāyana saw
the starting point of grasping.
He has indeed gone far beyond
Death’s dominion so hard to pass.

21.1.s:
Taṁ devadevaṁ vandāmi,
puttaṁ te dvipaduttama;
Anujātaṁ mahāvīraṁ,
nāgaṁ nāgassa orasan”ti.
21.1.e:
God of gods, best of men, I bow to you,
and to your son,
who followed your example, a great hero;
a giant, bosom son of a giant.”

21.1.s:
Sīhanādaṁ naditvāna,
buddhaputtā anāsavā;
Khemantaṁ pāpuṇitvāna,
aggikhandhāva nibbutāti.
